# Cassette — Product Vision & Research (2026 H1)

## 1. The vision in one paragraph

**Cassette is the offline trust substrate for the agentic stack: point it at any AI provider once, record the traffic, and then replay it byte-exact with the network unplugged — turning every LLM/SSE/MCP interaction into a portable, signed, auditable artifact you own and can replay, inspect, diff, and judge forever.** It is the local-first VCR for the agent inner loop — the tool you reach for to debug nondeterminism, reproduce a failure, run CI for free, prove what an agent did, and ship the same fixture to every teammate. Record once → replay forever → look at anything → check it holds. No SaaS, no key on replay, no egress, single static binary.

## 2. Where we fit — market map, wedge, and where we are NOT competing

The 2025–26 landscape splits cleanly into three camps, and cassette sits in the empty center none of them occupy.

**Gateways (Helicone, Portkey, Cloudflare, Braintrust)** cache responses to save cost/latency, but every cache is *live-network-tethered and not an artifact you own*. Cloudflare's cache is explicitly volatile and account-bound, with no self-host ([developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/)); Braintrust *deprecated* its proxy ([braintrust.dev/docs/guides/proxy](https://www.braintrust.dev/docs/guides/proxy)); Helicone still requires egress plus a funded account ([docs.helicone.ai/getting-started/quick-start](https://docs.helicone.ai/getting-started/quick-start)); Portkey's cache is an explicit live-network latency/cost optimization with a 7-day TTL ([portkey.ai/docs](https://portkey.ai/docs/introduction/what-is-portkey)). Helicone even normalizes volatile fields out of its cache key — conceptually the closest thing to cassette's match key — but it lives on Cloudflare's edge, not in a committable file ([docs.helicone.ai/features/advanced-usage/caching](https://docs.helicone.ai/features/advanced-usage/caching)).

**Observability/eval (Langfuse, Phoenix, OpenLLMetry, promptfoo)** captures lossy OTel *spans*, not replayable wire bytes. Langfuse's reproducibility comes from dataset versioning and re-runs against *live* models, not wire capture ([langfuse.com/docs](https://langfuse.com/docs)). Phoenix's "Span Replay" literally re-invokes the live model with your credentials — a naming collision with the *opposite* semantics of cassette ([arize.com/docs/phoenix](https://arize.com/docs/phoenix)). promptfoo is the closest philosophical neighbor (local-first eval CLI) but tests MCP/agents *live* and caches by response digest, with no SSE byte-capture, no offline guarantee, and errors not cached ([promptfoo.dev/docs/configuration/caching](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/configuration/caching/), [promptfoo.dev/docs/providers/mcp](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/providers/mcp/)).

**The new "VCR for LLM" swarm (reel-vcr, llmvcr, llm-vcr, llm_cassette, vcr-llm, Reel, agent-vcr)** validates the category but is uniformly v0.1.x, single-ecosystem, and shallow. vcr-llm *collapses streaming to non-streaming on replay* ([github.com/crithstudio-hash/vcr-llm](https://github.com/crithstudio-hash/vcr-llm)); agent-vcr does real MCP record/replay with 5 matchers and a breaking-change gate but ships **zero secret redaction** ([github.com/Jarvis2021/agent-vcr](https://github.com/Jarvis2021/agent-vcr)); the official MCP Inspector is live-only, in-memory, with no offline/committable replay ([github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector)).

**Our defensible wedge** is the intersection no one else holds: depth *and* breadth in one binary —
- **frame-exact SSE replay** with streamed tool-call reassembly (the swarm still collapses or only approximates this);
- **provable zero-egress** via the atomic dial counter — "the cache that works with the network unplugged";
- **HTTP/SSE *and* MCP stdio** unified in one artifact (the ecosystem currently splits these across two immature tools — Reel for HTTP, agent-vcr for MCP);
- **a cassette is simultaneously a fixture AND a governance object** — scrub-on-save, egress-audit, taint, and ed25519 attestation paired with byte-exact replay is a combination *no* competitor offers;
- **codec round-trip, cross-dialect transpile (no-drift gate), and offline judge-as-fixture eval** — the byte-reproducible determinism layer an eval can sit *on top of*.

**Where we are NOT competing:** we are not a hosted gateway, not a trace UI to rival Langfuse's polished dataset UX, and not a live-routing/load-balancing layer. Bare record/replay is now table stakes — we do not win there. We win on depth, on the unified HTTP+MCP artifact, and on being the *provable, offline, governable* substrate. We position inspect/dashboard/doc as **complementary** to the observability incumbents (we export to them; we don't out-UI them).

## 3. The cohesive product — ~60 commands as ONE product, anchored on REPLAY + inspect

The mental model is **one artifact, four verbs**: *everything you do is something you do to a cassette.* The cassette file is the single noun; commands are lenses on it.

| Verb | What it means | Folds in today's commands |
|------|---------------|---------------------------|
| **Capture** | get traffic into a cassette | `proxy`, `serve` (record), `author`, `scenario`, `fuzz` |
| **Replay** | the zero-egress core everything assumes | `serve` (replay), `pack`, CI mode, `watch` |
| **Look** | inspect / view / analyze | `inspect`, `doc`, `explain`, `diff`, `dashboard`, `coverage`, `shrink`, `bisect`, `doctor` |
| **Check** | prove it holds + govern it | `eval`, `scorecard`, `suite`, `ab`, `expect`/`assert`, `verify`, `attest`, `egress-audit`, `taint`, `redteam`, `cost`, `conformance`, `schema-check`, `lint` |
| *(Transform)* | reshape cassettes | `port`, `migrate`, `graft`, `distill`, `merge`/`stitch`/`split`/`stack`, `canonicalize` — surfaced as advanced power-tools under the verbs, not as 30 top-level peers |

The CLI and docs reorganize around these verbs. Power-tools live behind `cassette <verb>` namespaces; the ~60 commands stop being a flat sprawl and become a shallow, discoverable tree. The one-sentence story end-to-end: **record once → replay forever → look at anything → check it holds.**

**The "install once, point at your provider, it just works" setup story (concrete):**

The competitive bar is Cloudflare/Helicone's sub-2-minute, single-key first success ([docs.helicone.ai/getting-started/quick-start](https://docs.helicone.ai/getting-started/quick-start), [developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/get-started](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/get-started/)). We beat it decisively because **replay needs no key and no network at all** — a strictly lower-friction state than any gateway.

The single front door is **zero-config `cassette`** (no subcommand, no flags):
1. **Auto-pick a port** (and print the `base_url` to paste).
2. **Auto-detect the upstream** from the first request's Host/path (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible families all already supported).
3. **Auto-name the cassette** from the detected provider + date.
4. **Auto-choose record-vs-replay** via the existing `CASSETTE_MODE=auto`: if the cassette has the interaction, replay it offline; if not and a key is present, record it.

The user experience: *"Point your provider's `base_url` at cassette once. Record with your key. Then every teammate and every CI run replays byte-exact — zero key, zero network, forever."* Any required pre-step (naming, mode, upstream config) is friction to delete.

Two more pillars make it feel like one product:
- **`cassette open <file>` is the home** — one command launches the self-contained offline HTML dashboard *and* prints the transcript. It is the daily-loop entry point that unifies the scattered inspect/doc/explain/diff/dashboard surfaces.
- **`cassette doctor` is the safety net** — on a replay miss, cassette does not just error. It diagnoses: shows the closest recorded request, the exact field that broke the match key, and a one-line fix. This is the single biggest "it just works" lever for the debug loop.

## 4. Feature gaps to close (prioritized)

**P0 — Zero-config first run.** `cassette` with no flags must auto-pick port, auto-detect upstream, auto-name, auto-mode (§3). This is the entire "it just works" promise; nothing else matters if first-run has friction. *Effort: M* (mostly wiring existing `CASSETTE_MODE=auto` + Host detection into a flagless default path).

**P0 — `doctor` as the default failure path.** Replay misses should diagnose, not error — closest request, exact broken match-key field, one-line fix. Highest-leverage DX lever. *Effort: M* (the match key and normalization logic already exist; this is surfacing + diffing).

**P1 — Timing-faithful replay as a documented first-class mode.** Reel and llm_cassette now foreground inter-chunk SSE timing ([github.com/jibranusman95/llm_cassette](https://github.com/jibranusman95/llm_cassette)). Cassette's StreamTiming being off-by-default and silently dropped by `canonicalize` is now a positioning liability. Ship `--faithful-timing` as a supported, documented mode (keep off-by-default for fast CI, like llm_cassette does). *Effort: S–M* (data is already captured at frame level).

**P1 — `cassette inspect --otel` export.** Map a recorded cassette to OTel GenAI spans/metrics — `gen_ai.provider.name` (not the deprecated `gen_ai.system`), `gen_ai.usage.*`, `gen_ai.client.operation.time_to_first_chunk` — **including the MCP convention** (`mcp.client.operation.duration`, stdio + streamable-http). The conventions are still pre-stable, so this is a *wedge, not catch-up*, and it bridges into Langfuse/Phoenix/SigNoz instead of competing ([github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai)). *Effort: M.*

**P1 — MCP-axis matcher depth + breaking-change gate.** agent-vcr ships 5 matchers and a `--fail-on-breaking` CI diff gate ([github.com/Jarvis2021/agent-vcr](https://github.com/Jarvis2021/agent-vcr)). Match that rigor on MCP sessions where we already lead on safety (redaction/attestation, which agent-vcr lacks entirely). *Effort: M.*

**P2 — Documented portable cassette spec for cross-language replay-as-fixture.** The format is Go-library-bound; the proxy makes *recording* any-language, but replaying a cassette as a fixture inside a non-Go test suite needs a documented spec (agent-vcr's plain-JSON format gives it cross-language portability). *Effort: M–L.*

## 5. What more we can bring (net-new, ranked by leverage)

1. **`cassette audit` — a one-command compliance bundle.** Emit a signed, dated evidence pack: attestation manifest + egress-audit PII report + taint flow trace + coverage matrix, as a single portable file. This is the SOC2 / EU AI Act / ISO 42001 deliverable auditors actually ask for, generated from artifacts we already hold. Highest leverage because it opens an entirely new buyer (governance/GRC) with near-zero new primitives. *Leverage: very high.*

2. **Cassette-as-backend for promptfoo.** promptfoo runs MCP/agents *live* with a non-guaranteed disk cache ([promptfoo.dev/docs/providers/mcp](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/providers/mcp/)). Ship a cassette provider/cache adapter so a promptfoo eval sits *on top of* deterministic, offline replay. Distribution into the leading local-first eval tool's user base. *Leverage: high.*

3. **Policy gate (`cassette.policy.yaml`).** A declarative policy (no secrets, no PII class X, must attest, must not exceed cost budget) enforced at save-time and in CI. Turns the scattered verify/egress-audit/taint/cost commands into one guardrail. *Leverage: high.*

4. **Provenance chain.** Cryptographically link record → scrub → port → eval so a replayed result carries its full lineage: "this eval ran against *these exact bytes*, scrubbed by *this policy*, signed *here*." Deepens the moat the swarm can't touch. *Leverage: medium-high.*

5. **`cassette open` as the unified offline viewer** (also a P1 in §3) — beyond launching, make it the canonical "MCP Inspector you can commit" surface: step through a saved MCP session, diff two sessions, sign the result. *Leverage: medium-high.*

## 6. New areas to service (adjacent domains, with evidence + wedge)

1. **Regulated & air-gapped AI (finance, healthcare, defense, gov).** *Wedge:* zero-egress replay is the *only* way to run, test, or demo AI where network egress is forbidden. No gateway works here (all need egress + accounts); no observability tool replays offline. "The AI fixture that works inside the airgap" has no competitor. *Evidence:* every gateway surveyed requires live egress ([Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/), [Helicone](https://docs.helicone.ai/getting-started/quick-start)).

2. **AI compliance & audit tooling (EU AI Act, SOC2, ISO 42001).** *Wedge:* reproducibility + provenance + signed behavioral manifests are becoming legal/audit requirements; cassette is the evidence-generation layer beneath any GRC workflow (powered by `audit`, §5). *Evidence:* attestation + egress-audit + taint exist today and no eval/gateway tool pairs them with replay.

3. **MCP server conformance & regression testing.** *Wedge:* as MCP servers proliferate, a committable golden cassette + breaking-change diff gate becomes the CI primitive for "did my server change behavior?" The official Inspector leaves this open (live-only, no persistence — [github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector)); agent-vcr has the gate but no redaction. We hold both. *Evidence:* the OTel MCP convention being first-class validates MCP as a durable axis ([semantic-conventions-genai](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai)).

4. **Free, hermetic CI for agent teams.** *Wedge:* record once with a key; every teammate and every CI run replays with zero key, zero egress, zero flake. Sell the *team outcome*, not the primitive — this is the adoption flywheel. *Evidence:* the swarm proves demand for record/replay but none offer provable zero-network team-shareable fixtures.

5. **Incident forensics / model-swap diffing.** *Wedge:* a signed recording is a tamper-evident record of "what the model actually did" — for post-incident review, refusal regressions, and vendor-swap risk (redteam/ab over recorded bytes). *Evidence:* Phoenix/Langfuse capture lossy spans, not byte-exact wire — they cannot serve as forensic ground truth ([arize.com/docs/phoenix](https://arize.com/docs/phoenix)).

## 7. Risks & non-goals

**Risks:**
- **Category commoditization.** "VCR for LLM" is now crowded at the basic record/replay layer. *Mitigation:* compete only on depth (codec round-trip, transpile, judge-as-fixture, attestation, taint) and the unified HTTP+MCP artifact — never on the bare primitive.
- **"Replay" naming collision.** Phoenix "Span Replay" and MCP Inspector "Pin and Replay" both mean *live re-invocation*. *Mitigation:* explicitly disambiguate in all positioning — "offline, byte-exact, network-unplugged replay."
- **MCP-axis threat.** agent-vcr is more featured on pure MCP matching/diffing. *Mitigation:* close the matcher/gate gap (§4 P1) fast, and lean on redaction + attestation, which it entirely lacks.
- **Standards drift.** OTel GenAI field names are still moving (`gen_ai.system` → `gen_ai.provider.name`). *Mitigation:* treat the export as pre-stable and version it.

**Non-goals (deliberately NOT doing):**
- **Hosted dashboard / web UI / SaaS** — the offline single binary is the identity. Keep the dashboard self-contained and local.
- **Live routing / load-balancing / gateway-style fallbacks** — that is the gateways' game; we are the offline substrate underneath.
- **LIVE judging** — the judge-as-fixture being itself a recorded cassette is the whole point of byte-reproducibility. (`watch` stays an explicit opt-in live drift probe only.)
- **Native pip/npm SDKs** — keep the Go library + any-language proxy. *Revisit candidate:* a **documented portable cassette spec** (§4 P2) gets most of the cross-language value without owning N SDKs.
- **Plugin system, realtime voice/vision/gRPC, SQL query engine, MITM CA daemon** — remain out of scope; revisit only if a named buyer in §6 demands one.

## 8. Suggested roadmap (sequenced, opinionated)

**Move 1 — Win the front door (P0, this cycle).** Ship zero-config `cassette` (auto port/upstream/name/mode) + `doctor`-on-miss + `cassette open` as the unified viewer. This is the "it just works" promise and the daily-loop home. Everything else compounds on adoption from here.

**Move 2 — Lock the wedges that are turning into liabilities (P1).** Timing-faithful replay as a documented mode; MCP matcher depth + `--fail-on-breaking` gate. Neutralizes the two places competitors are catching up or ahead.

**Move 3 — Bridge the ecosystem (P1).** `cassette inspect --otel` (incl. MCP convention) + the promptfoo cassette-backend adapter. Turns cassette from a standalone tool into the substrate *under* the observability and eval stacks — distribution without competing.

**Move 4 — Open the governance buyer (net-new, high leverage).** `cassette audit` bundle + `cassette.policy.yaml` gate + provenance chain. Converts existing security primitives into a new market (regulated/air-gapped/compliance) with minimal new engineering.

**Move 5 — Platform/network effects (P2).** Documented portable cassette spec → signed, scrubbed, shareable corpora (refusal sets, red-team suites, judge fixtures) that any team replays byte-identically. This is the long-game registry play once the substrate is beloved.

Sequencing rationale: 1 buys adoption, 2 defends the moat, 3 distributes through incumbents, 4 opens a new buyer cheaply, 5 builds the network effect last — when there's a base to network.
